sources.speedPower: z(fitted BPM) + 0.35 * z(fitted VORP per game), mapped onto the finished set's Speed+Power distribution with the current NBA pool as the calibration basis. Both sides of that map are scored with the SAME fitted model, so its compression cancels.
sources.bpm: FITTED. Basketball-Reference publishes no BPM, OBPM, DBPM or VORP for the WNBA. The model is regressed on 15 NBA seasons using only inputs the WNBA pages also carry, every input centred on its own league-season mean. See card-data/generated/wnba-bpm-model.json for the out-of-sample R² and what real BPM uses that this cannot.
sources.defBoost: the fitted DBPM, rounded — the special sets' rule on a fitted input
sources.paintBoost: 2P% standing in for rim FG%, which Basketball-Reference does not carry for either league
sources.shotLine: real WNBA TS%, compressed onto the finished set's Shot Line distribution using the WNBA POOL as the compression basis, so a league-wide shooting offset cancels instead of becoming a flat balance change
sources.chart: synthesized from Basketball-Reference WNBA season TOTALS: production per four-minute section is 4 * total / minutes, measured, with no pace in it. For reference, a 40-minute WNBA game at the measured 2026 league pace of 79.24 possessions per 40 minutes makes a four-minute section 7.924 possessions, against the NBA convention's 8.333 — which is what a per-100 rate would have had to be read against, and what carries each team’s own pace as error. Same synthesis model as the base set.

note: PROVISIONAL, and league-relative by design. Every cross-league number here says where a player stands in HER OWN league, placed on the NBA set's scale so the cards can share a table. It is not a claim that the leagues are equally strong; no published data could settle that.
